chunks: As for what Ibn Muskan narrated from Abi Basir, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, he said:

Nothing cuts off the salat (prayer): neither a dog, nor a donkey, nor a woman. But screen yourselves with something; if there is before you, to the measure of a forearm, something raised from the ground, then you have screened yourself.

key_terms.ذِرَاعٍ: a forearm-length measure used to describe the height or extent
key_terms.رَافِعٌ: something raised up from the ground
key_terms.يَقْطَعُ: invalidates or cuts off the continuity of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱسْتَتَرْتَ: you have screened yourself with a barrier
key_terms.ٱسْتَتِرُوا: use a screen or barrier in front of yourselves during salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةَ: the ritual salat (prayer) being discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Does anything like a dog, donkey, or woman passing in front of a person invalidate the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the passing of a dog, donkey, or woman does not invalidate the salat (prayer). It instructs the worshipper to place a sutrah-like barrier in front, and explains that an object raised from the ground by about a forearm's measure fulfills that purpose.
